The API Trigger node lets you initiate outbound calls to your voice agent programmatically. When you add an API Trigger node to your workflow, Verasist generates a unique endpoint URL that external systems can call to start a conversation.

This is useful when you want to trigger calls from your own backend, a CRM, or workflow tools like n8n and Zapier.

Prerequisites

  • A configured telephony provider — outbound calls will fail without one
  • An API key for authentication

Finding your trigger URL

When you add an API Trigger node to your workflow, Verasist assigns it a unique UUID. The trigger node exposes two URLs that share this UUID:

  • A production URL for the published workflow
  • A test URL for the latest draft
You can copy either URL from the trigger node's settings dialog. 
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid}        # Production
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid}   # Test

If you are using the hosted version, replace verasist.ai with api.verasist.ai.

Test vs production

Mode URL Runs
Production /api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} The published version of the agent.
Test /api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} The latest draft. Falls back to the published version if no draft exists.

Use the test URL while iterating on changes so production traffic continues to hit the published version.

The production URL only executes a published workflow. If you update the workflow but do not publish it, the production trigger will continue to run the older published version.

Once you publish your draft, both URLs run the same definition.

A common pitfall is editing the workflow, saving the draft, and then calling the production trigger URL expecting the new behavior. That will not work until you publish the workflow. Use the test URL to verify draft changes before publishing.

The request body, headers, and response shape are identical for both URLs.

Channels

By default, an API Trigger node launches a phone call, but the node can be configured for a different channel — whatsapp, telegram, instagram, or text — and a request can override that channel per call by passing channel in the request body.

channel Required request fields Response message
phone (default) phone_number null
whatsapp / telegram / instagram target (destination identity for that channel), channel_configuration_id (unless the node has one configured) The workflow's first generated reply
text — The workflow's first generated reply
text starts the workflow without any external channel — the response body itself contains the agent's first message, useful for embedding the agent in your own UI without setting up a channel integration.

``bash WhatsApp channel curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "channel": "whatsapp", "target": "+14155550100", "channel_configuration_id": 12, "initial_context": {"customer_name": "Jane"} }' 


channel is required in the request body when neither the node nor the request otherwise specify one — for example when triggering by workflow UUID directly, which has no node to fall back to.


Making a request


Authenticate by passing your API key in the X-API-Key header. For the default phone channel, the request body requires a phone_number and accepts optional initial_context and telephony_configuration_id fields (see Channels above for the fields required by other channels).
bash Production URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }'
bash Test URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }' 


Use the test URL when you want to verify draft changes before publishing.


Response


A successful request returns a workflow_run_id that you can use to retrieve run details, recordings, and transcripts.
json { "status": "initiated", "workflow_run_id": 12345, "workflow_run_name": "WR-API-7823" } 


Error responses






Status
Cause






400
Telephony provider not configured, or call failed to initiate




401
Missing or invalid API key




403
API key does not have access to this agent




404
Trigger not found or not active






Initial context


initial_context is a JSON object containing any information you want your voice agent to access during the call. You can reference these values in your prompts using template variables — values enclosed in {{ and }}.


For example, if your request includes:
json { "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "user": { "name": "John" } } } 

You can reference the user's name in your agent prompt as {{user.name}} — in Agent prompts, initial_context fields are referenced directly by name (not prefixed with initial_context.). See template variables for the exact syntax in prompts versus webhook payloads.


See Context & Variables for more on how data flows through a call.


Choosing a telephony configuration


By default, calls are placed through your organization's default outbound telephony configuration. To route a specific call through a different configuration — for example, to dial out from a regional number — pass telephony_configuration_id in the request body.
json { "phone_number": "+14155550100", "telephony_configuration_id": 42 } `

The id is shown on each row in Telephony configurations (https://app.verasist.ai/telephony-configurations). The configuration must belong to the same organization as the API Trigger; otherwise the request returns 404`.

For full endpoint details including all parameters and response fields, see the API reference.

You can embed your Verasist agent on any website in two ways:

  • Voice — visitors click a button and talk to your agent through their microphone, with real-time WebRTC audio streaming
  • Text chat — visitors type messages and your agent replies, just like a chat widget
Both modes use the same embed snippet and the same three rendering options below. The widget automatically detects which mode your workflow supports and adapts its UI accordingly — a microphone button for voice agents, a chat input for text agents.

How to add it

Add your voice agent to any website using the Configure Widget dialog in your agent's settings.

Step 1: Open the agent settings by clicking the gear icon in the top-right of the agent editor.

Step 2: Scroll to the Add to Website section and click Configure Widget.

Step 3: Enable embedding, add your website's domain to Allowed Domains, choose Floating Widget, Inline Component, or Headless (Bring Your Own UI), customize the button (position, color, text) if applicable, and click Save Configurations.

Step 4: Copy the generated embed code and paste it into your web page to test your agent.

Embed modes

Mode What it renders When to use
Floating Widget A pill-shaped CTA button anchored to a corner of the page. You want a turn-key chat-bubble experience that doesn't disturb your existing layout.
Inline Component A panel rendered inside a
that you place in your page.
 You want the agent embedded in a specific section (landing-page hero, support tab, etc.).
Headless No UI. Only the audio pipeline plus a JavaScript API on window.VerasistWidget. You want full control over the UI — your own buttons, design system, framework state, animations.

Prerequisites

These apply to all three modes:

  • Serve your page over HTTPS. Browsers refuse microphone access on plain HTTP origins or file://.
  • If you set Allowed Domains in the dashboard, include your test origin (e.g. test.your-app.example) — otherwise the widget's config and signaling requests are rejected. Leave the list empty to allow all domains.
  • The embed snippet you copy from the dashboard is a single

    React + TypeScript

    import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

    type CallStatus = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'connected' | 'failed';
    

    declare global {
  interface Window {
    VerasistWidget: {
      start: () => void;
      end: () => void;
      onStatusChange: (cb: (status: CallStatus, text?: string, subtext?: string) => void) => void;
      onError: (cb: (err: Error) => void) => void;
    };
  }
}
    

    export function TalkButton() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('idle');
    

    useEffect(() => {
    window.VerasistWidget.onStatusChange((s) => setStatus(s));
    window.VerasistWidget.onError((err) => console.error('Verasist error:', err.message));
  }, []);
    

    const isLive = status === 'connected' || status === 'connecting';
  const label = { idle: 'Talk to AI', connecting: 'Connecting…', connected: 'End Call', failed: 'Retry' }[status];
    

    return (
    
  );
}

    start() must run inside a real user-gesture handler (click, touchend, etc.). Browsers refuse to grant microphone access to scripts that request it outside of one — calling start() from a setTimeout or on page load will fail with a permission error.

    Lifecycle callbacks (all modes)

    The on* callbacks in the Headless JavaScript API work in all three embed modes, not just Headless. Use them for analytics or to trigger UI in the host page even when the widget is rendering its own UI (Floating or Inline).

    window.VerasistWidget.onCallConnected(({ agentId, workflowRunId }) => {
  analytics.track('voice_call_started', { agentId, workflowRunId });
});

    window.VerasistWidget.onCallDisconnected(({ workflowRunId, durationSeconds }) => {
  analytics.track('voice_call_ended', { workflowRunId, durationSeconds });
});

    onCallConnected and onCallDisconnected only fire when the session actually establishes a connection — failed-to-connect attempts (e.g. denied mic, network failure) don't trigger them, so analytics stay clean.

Verasist handles two types of recordings:

  1. Call recordings — audio captured during live phone calls, stored automatically after each call ends
  2. Pre-recorded audio — files you upload to use in your workflows (e.g., greeting messages, hold music, sound effects)

Call recordings

Every voice call is recorded end-to-end. After the call ends, the recording is processed and stored in your organization's storage (S3-compatible MinIO or cloud storage).

Accessing recordings

Navigate to Recordings (/recordings) in the sidebar (under the Build section).

The page lists all call recordings with:

Column Description
Date When the call took place
Workflow Which agent handled the call
Caller Phone number of the caller
Duration Length of the call
Status Processing status (ready, processing, failed)
Actions Download, play, or delete

Playing and downloading

  • Play inline: Click the play button to listen to the recording directly in your browser
  • Download: Download the audio file for external analysis, compliance archiving, or sharing
  • Delete: Remove recordings you no longer need

Recording format

  • Format: Standard audio format (MP3 or WAV)
  • Storage: Recordings are stored securely in your organization's dedicated storage bucket
  • Retention: Managed by your platform administrator's storage policy

Recording from run details

You can also access the recording from any individual run:

  1. Go to Workflows → select a workflow → Runs tab
  2. Click on a specific run
  3. In the run detail view, find the Recording section with play/download options
The run detail view also shows the context that flowed through the call:
  • Initial context — data passed into the call before it started (e.g., customer name from a campaign CSV, account details from a pre-call API fetch)
  • Gathered context — structured data the agent extracted during the conversation (e.g., call disposition, appointment date, customer intent)
This lets you verify what the agent knew going in and what it learned by the end. See Context & Variables for how to configure extraction in your workflows.

Pre-recorded audio

Pre-recorded audio files are different from call recordings — you upload these yourself to use them during calls. This is useful for:

  • Branded greetings: A professionally recorded welcome message
  • Hold music: Background music while processing
  • Sound effects: Notification chimes, confirmation tones
  • Multi-language messages: Pre-recorded translations instead of TTS

Uploading pre-recorded audio

  1. Go to Recordings (/recordings)
  2. Click Upload
  3. Select your audio file
  4. Give it a descriptive name
  5. The file is now available in your workflow's pre-recorded audio selector

Using in workflows

Once uploaded, pre-recorded audio can be used in:

  • Start Call nodes — replace the initial greeting with a recording
  • Agent nodes — play a recording at a specific conversation point
  • End Call nodes — play a closing message
See Pre-recorded Audio for workflow configuration details.

Storage & retention

Aspect Detail
Storage backend Secure cloud storage
Organization isolation Each organization's recordings are stored in a dedicated bucket/prefix
Access control Only members of your organization can access your recordings
Retention policy Set by your platform administrator

Troubleshooting

Recording not showing up after a callRecordings are processed asynchronously after the call ends. If it's been more than a few minutes, the recording may have failed to process — check the run detail page for any error indicators.
Recording is silent or incompleteThis can happen if the call dropped unexpectedly or the audio stream was interrupted. Check the call's connection logs in the run detail page for any network issues during the call.
Can't upload pre-recorded audioEnsure the file is in a supported format. Check your organization's storage quota with your administrator.

Overview

Verasist AI supports inbound calling across all supported telephony providers. When someone calls your configured phone number, your voice agent automatically answers and handles the interaction. Inbound and outbound calls share the same telephony configuration.

Supported Providers for Inbound Calls

Industry-leading platform with robust inbound call handling Application-level inbound routing with high-quality 16kHz audio Application-level inbound routing on Plivo's global voice cloud Application-level inbound via Telnyx Call Control API SIP-based inbound calling with flexible trunk configuration Cloud-based telephony with global reach and competitive pricing Bring your own SIP trunk from NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, or any standards-compliant provider

How Inbound Calling Works

Verasist exposes a single inbound webhook URL for the whole org:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run

When a call arrives:

  1. Call Received: Your telephony provider receives the incoming call
  2. Webhook Triggered: The provider sends a webhook to /inbound/run
  3. Org & Agent Resolved: Verasist identifies the org from the webhook's account credentials, then looks up which agent should answer based on the called number's Inbound workflow assignment in your telephony configuration
  4. Audio Streaming: Real-time audio streams between caller and agent via WebSocket
  5. Conversation Handled: Your voice agent manages the entire conversation
You don't construct per-workflow URLs anymore — the routing is done by the called number's inbound workflow assignment in Verasist.

Configuration in Verasist AI

Setting up inbound calling takes three steps:

Step 1: Configure Telephony Provider

The telephony configuration for inbound calling is identical to outbound calling. Add (or open) a configuration at /telephony-configurations following your provider's documentation:

  • Twilio Configuration
  • Vonage Configuration
  • Plivo Configuration
  • Telnyx Configuration
  • Cloudonix Configuration
  • Vobiz Configuration
  • SIP Trunk Configuration

Step 2: Assign an Inbound Workflow to the Phone Number

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save
This is what tells Verasist which agent to run when a call comes in for that number.

Step 3: Point Your Provider at /inbound/run

Each provider needs its inbound webhook (Twilio Voice URL / Vonage Answer URL / etc.) set to the global Verasist endpoint:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run

The exact place to set this varies by provider — follow the provider-specific instructions:

  • Twilio Inbound Setup
  • Vonage Inbound Setup
  • Plivo Inbound Setup
  • Telnyx Inbound Setup
  • Cloudonix Inbound Setup
  • Vobiz Inbound Setup
  • SIP Trunk Inbound Setup

Testing Inbound Calls

After completing both the Verasist AI configuration and provider-specific setup:

  1. Test Call: Call your configured phone number from another phone
  2. Verify Connection: Ensure your voice agent answers and responds appropriately
  3. Check Logs: Monitor call logs in both Verasist AI and your provider's dashboard
  4. Audio Quality: Verify clear two-way audio communication

Troubleshooting Common Issues

Calls go to voicemail instead of agent- Verify webhook URLs are correctly configured at your provider - Check that webhook endpoints are publicly accessible - Ensure phone numbers are properly linked to your application
Agent doesn't respond to incoming calls- Confirm your voice agent workflow is properly configured - Check webhook signature validation is working - Verify WebSocket connections are established successfully
Provider mismatch error- Error: "Configuration error: This phone number is configured for a different telephony provider" - Solution: Check your dashboard settings and update your webhook URL configuration to match the correct provider - Ensure the phone number is configured for the same provider in both Verasist AI and your telephony console
Workflow not found error- Error: "Workflow not found" - Solution: Open the called number in /telephony-configurations and confirm an Inbound workflow is assigned. Without an assignment, Verasist has no agent to route the call to. - Verify the assigned workflow still exists in your dashboard
Account validation failed- Error: "Authentication error: Account credentials do not match" - Solution: Verify your account SID/credentials configuration in Verasist AI matches your telephony provider settings - Re-enter your provider credentials in the telephony configuration page
Phone number not configured- Error: "Phone number not configured: This number is not set up for inbound calls" - Solution: Add this phone number under Phone numbers in your telephony configuration at /telephony-configurations - Ensure the phone number is also linked to your provider account
Signature validation failed- Error: "Security error: Webhook signature validation failed" - Solution: Verify your auth token configuration in Verasist AI matches your provider settings - Ensure webhook requests are coming from your telephony provider's verified IP ranges - Check that your webhook URL is accessible and responding correctly
Quota exceeded error- Error: "Service temporarily unavailable: Your account has exceeded usage limits" - Solution: Contact your administrator or upgrade your plan to continue receiving calls - Check your provider account billing and usage limits
General authentication failed- Error: "Authentication failed" - Solution: Check your webhook URL configuration and ensure your telephony provider settings match your dashboard configuration - Verify all credentials are entered correctly and haven't expired - Test the webhook URL is publicly accessible from your provider's servers
Poor audio quality on inbound calls- Check network bandwidth and latency from provider to Verasist AI - Verify audio pipeline configuration matches provider requirements - Review WebSocket connection stability

Best Practices

  • Single Configuration: Use the same telephony configuration for both inbound and outbound calls
  • Testing: Always test inbound calling after configuration changes
  • Monitoring: Monitor both Verasist AI logs and provider dashboards for call analytics
  • Security: Ensure webhook signature verification is enabled for security

Next Steps

  1. Choose your telephony provider and complete the basic configuration
  2. Follow the provider-specific setup instructions
  3. Assign an inbound workflow to each phone number that should accept calls
  4. Test your inbound calling setup

Overview

Twilio is a cloud communications platform that enables voice calling, messaging, and video capabilities. Verasist AI's Twilio integration provides seamless connectivity for your voice agents.

Prerequisites

Before setting up Twilio integration, you'll need:

  • A Twilio account
  • Account SID and Auth Token from your Twilio Console
  • At least one Twilio phone number
  • Verasist AI instance running and accessible

Configuration

Step 1: Get Twilio Credentials

  1. Log in to your Twilio Console
  2. Find your Account SID and Auth Token on the dashboard
  3. Navigate to Phone Numbers → Manage → Active Numbers
  4. Copy your phone number(s)

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select Twilio as your provider
  3. Enter your credentials:
- Account SID - Auth Token
  1. Click Save Configuration
  2. Open the configuration you just created and add at least one phone number (with country code in E.164 format, e.g. +1234567890). The default caller ID is used for outbound calls.

Step 3: Test Your Configuration

  1. Create a test workflow
  2. Click "Call" to verify connection
  3. Check call logs for successful connection

Inbound Calling Setup

Inbound routing is driven by the phone number itself — there is a single webhook URL for the entire org, and Verasist resolves which agent to run from the called number's assigned inbound workflow. When you save an inbound workflow on a phone number, Verasist automatically pushes the webhook URL to that number's VoiceUrl in your Twilio account (provided the credentials are correct and the number belongs to that account).

Step 1: Assign an Inbound Workflow to the Phone Number

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your Twilio configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Step 2: Verify the Webhook URL in Twilio Console

  1. Go to Phone Numbers → Manage → Active Numbers in Twilio Console
  2. Click the phone number you assigned an inbound workflow to in Step 1
  3. In the Voice Configuration section, confirm:
- Webhook is set to: https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - HTTP Method is POST
Verasist pushed this URL automatically when you saved the inbound workflow in Step 1. If the field is empty, shows a different URL, or Verasist surfaced a sync warning, the auto-push failed — most often because the credentials are incorrect or the number isn't owned by this Twilio account. Paste the URL into the field yourself, set the method to POST, and click Save Configuration.

### Step 3: Verify Setup

  • Ensure your Verasist AI instance is publicly accessible
  • Verify any firewalls allow Twilio's IP ranges

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured Twilio phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI voice agent answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in both Verasist AI dashboard and Twilio Console

Troubleshooting

Invalid phone number errorEnsure phone numbers include country code in E.164 format: +1234567890
Authentication failed- Verify Account SID and Auth Token are correct - Check for extra spaces in credentials - Ensure credentials haven't been regenerated in Twilio Console
Webhook signature validation failing- Confirm your Auth Token matches exactly - Verify the webhook URL matches what Twilio sends - Check if you're behind a proxy that modifies requests
No audio on calls- Verify WebSocket connection is established - Check firewall rules for WebSocket traffic - Ensure audio pipeline is configured correctly
Inbound calls go to voicemail- Verify the Twilio number's webhook is set to https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - Ensure the webhook URL is publicly accessible from the internet - Confirm the called number exists in your Verasist telephony configuration and has an **Inbound workflow** assigned - Verify Verasist AI instance is running and responding
Voice agent doesn't respond to inbound calls- Confirm the phone number has an Inbound workflow assigned in /telephony-configurations - Check webhook signature validation is working (Auth Token in Verasist matches Twilio Console) - Verify WebSocket connection establishes successfully - Review call logs for error messages

Best Practices

  • Test your configuration with a single call before running campaigns
  • Monitor Twilio Console for usage and billing

Overview

Vonage (formerly Nexmo) is a cloud communications platform that provides global voice, messaging, and video capabilities. Verasist AI's Vonage integration enables high-quality voice interactions with your agents using Vonage's robust infrastructure.

Prerequisites

Before setting up Vonage integration, you'll need:

  • A Vonage account
  • Vonage Application with Voice capability enabled
  • Application ID and Private Key from your Vonage Dashboard
  • API Key and API Secret from your Vonage Dashboard
  • At least one Vonage phone number linked to the application
  • Verasist AI instance running and accessible

Configuration

Step 1: Create Vonage Application

  1. Log in to your Vonage Dashboard
  2. Navigate to Applications → Create a new application
  3. Enable Voice capability
  4. Generate a private key (save this securely - you'll need it)
  5. Note your Application ID

Step 2: Get API Credentials

  1. Find your API Key and API Secret in the dashboard under API Settings
  2. Navigate to Numbers → Your Numbers
  3. Copy your phone number(s)
  4. Link your numbers to your application

Step 3: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select Vonage as your provider
  3. Enter your credentials:
- Application ID - Private Key (entire key including BEGIN/END lines) - API Key - API Secret
  1. Click Save Configuration
  2. Open the configuration you just created and add at least one phone number (without + prefix, e.g. 14155551234). The default caller ID is used for outbound calls.

Step 4: Test Your Configuration

  1. Create a test workflow
  2. Click "Call" to verify connection
  3. Check call logs for successful connection

Inbound Calling Setup

Vonage configures inbound webhooks at the application level, not per phone number. A single Answer URL on the Vonage application applies to every number linked to it. Verasist routes the call to the right agent based on the called number's inbound workflow assignment inside Verasist. When you save an inbound workflow on a phone number, Verasist automatically pushes the webhook URL to your Vonage Application's Answer URL (provided the credentials are correct).

Step 1: Link Phone Numbers to Your Vonage Application

  1. Open the Vonage Dashboard
  2. Under Numbers → Your Numbers, link each number you want to use for inbound to the same Vonage Application whose ID you configured in Verasist

Step 2: Assign an Inbound Workflow to the Phone Number in Verasist

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your Vonage configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Step 3: Verify the Answer URL on the Vonage Application

  1. Open your Vonage Application in the Vonage Dashboard
  2. Under Capabilities → Voice, confirm:
- Answer URL is set to: https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - HTTP Method is POST
Verasist pushed this URL automatically when you saved the inbound workflow in Step 2. If the field is empty, shows a different URL, or Verasist surfaced a sync warning on save, the auto-push failed — most often because the API Key/Secret or Application ID in Verasist is incorrect. Paste the URL into the field yourself, set the method to POST, and save the application.

Step 4: Verify Setup

  • Ensure your Verasist AI instance is publicly accessible
  • Verify any firewalls allow Vonage's IP ranges

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured Vonage phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI voice agent answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in both Verasist AI dashboard and Vonage Dashboard

Audio Quality Optimization

Vonage uses higher quality audio (16kHz) which provides:

  • Clearer voice reproduction
  • Better speech recognition accuracy
  • More natural-sounding TTS output
  • Reduced transcription errors

Troubleshooting

Voice application capabilities error- Ensure "Voice" is enabled in your Vonage application - Verify the application ID matches your configuration - Check that your phone numbers are linked to the application
JWT authentication failed- Verify your private key is complete (including BEGIN/END lines) - Check the Application ID is correct - Ensure the private key hasn't been regenerated in Vonage Dashboard
Invalid phone number error- Remove the '+' prefix for Vonage (use 14155551234 not +14155551234) - Ensure numbers are in E.164 format without the '+' - Verify numbers are active in your Vonage account
No audio on calls- Verify WebSocket connection is established - Check audio pipeline is configured for 16kHz PCM - Monitor WebSocket for binary audio frames - Review VAD (Voice Activity Detection) settings
Calls disconnecting early- Check WebSocket heartbeat/ping-pong frames - Verify no timeout in load balancer/proxy - Monitor for audio pipeline errors - Review max call duration settings
Inbound calls not reaching voice agent- Verify the Vonage application's Answer URL is set to https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - Ensure the Answer URL is publicly accessible - Confirm the called number is linked to the correct Vonage application - Confirm the called number exists in your Verasist telephony configuration and has an Inbound workflow assigned
Voice agent doesn't respond to inbound calls- Confirm the phone number has an Inbound workflow assigned in /telephony-configurations - Verify API Key matches the one stored in your Verasist telephony configuration (used to identify the org from the inbound webhook) - Verify WebSocket connection establishes successfully - Review call logs for error messages

Best Practices

  • Security: Private keys are stored securely in the database
  • Testing: Use Vonage Voice Inspector for debugging call issues
  • Numbers: Configure multiple numbers for redundancy
  • Monitoring: Set up alerts in Vonage Dashboard for failures
  • Cost Management: Monitor usage to control costs

Cost Considerations

Vonage pricing includes:

  • Per-minute charges for calls
  • Phone number rental fees
  • Optional features (recording, transcription)
Check Vonage pricing for current rates.

Next Steps

  • Test your Vonage integration with a simple workflow
  • Configure VAD settings for optimal voice detection
  • Set up monitoring and alerts
  • Explore advanced features like call recording

Overview

Plivo is a cloud communications platform that provides global voice and messaging APIs. Verasist AI's Plivo integration uses Plivo's XML and WebSocket streaming to power your voice agents.

Prerequisites

Before setting up Plivo integration, you'll need:

  • A Plivo account
  • Auth ID and Auth Token from your Plivo Console
  • A Plivo Application with Voice capability (optional — leave the field blank in Verasist and we'll auto-create one for you on save, with the answer_url pre-set)
  • At least one Plivo phone number
  • Verasist AI instance running and accessible

Configuration

Step 1: Get Plivo Credentials

  1. Log in to your Plivo Console
  2. Find your Auth ID and Auth Token on the dashboard
  3. (Optional) Navigate to Voice → Applications and create (or open) the application you'll use with Verasist, then copy its Application ID (a UUID). Skip this if you want Verasist to auto-create the application for you on save.
  4. Navigate to Phone Numbers → Your Numbers and copy the numbers you plan to use

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select Plivo as your provider
  3. Enter your credentials:
- Auth ID - Auth Token - Application ID — optional. Leave blank and Verasist will auto-create a Plivo Application on save (with the answer_url already configured) and store its Application ID on this configuration.
  1. Click Save Configuration

Verasist AI supports external SIP trunk providers through its built-in Asterisk PJSIP stack. When you configure a SIP trunk, Verasist handles all call control (origination, bridging, teardown) automatically — you only need to provide your provider's SIP credentials.

Supported SIP trunk providers include: NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, Flowroute, Vobiz, and any standards-compliant SIP trunk provider.

Prerequisites

  • An active SIP trunk from a supported provider (NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, Flowroute, Vobiz, etc.)
  • SIP credentials from your provider:
- Gateway IP / Hostname — The provider's SIP server address - Username & Password — SIP authentication credentials - From User / Caller ID (optional) — The number or user shown on outbound calls - DID Numbers — The phone numbers assigned to your trunk
  • Your provider must allow traffic from the Verasist server IP (see Firewall & IP Whitelisting)

Configuration

Step 1: Obtain SIP Trunk Credentials

  1. Sign up with your SIP trunk provider (NetGSM, Verimor, etc.)
  2. Obtain from your provider:
- Gateway IP / Hostname — The provider's SIP server address (e.g. sip.netgsm.com.tr) - Username & Password — SIP authentication credentials - From User / Caller ID (optional) — The caller identity for outbound calls. Defaults to username if not set. - DID Numbers — The phone numbers assigned to your trunk
  1. Note whether your provider requires SIP registration (register: true) or uses IP-based authentication (register: false). Most providers (NetGSM, Verimor) require registration.

Step 2: IP Whitelisting (Kritik Önemli)

Most SIP trunk providers (NetGSM, Verimor, etc.) require you to whitelist the server IP that will send/receive SIP traffic. This is a security measure — without it, your provider will reject SIP registration and inbound/outbound calls will fail. Yapmanız gerekenler:
  1. Verasist sunucunuzun public IP adresini öğrenin
  2. SIP trunk sağlayıcınızın yönetim paneline giriş yapın:
- NetGSM: "Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama" veya "Güvenlik" menüsünden IP ekleyin - Verimor: Müşteri panelinden IP whitelist bölümüne gidin - Diğer sağlayıcılar: İlgili güvenlik / firewall / allowed IPs ayarlarını bulun
  1. Verasist sunucunuzun public IP'sini listeye ekleyin
  2. Değişikliğin yayılmasını bekleyin (genellikle anında, bazen birkaç dakika)

Firewall & IP Whitelisting

When using a SIP Trunk provider, you must whitelist the Verasist server's public IP address on your provider's side. This is critical because:

  • SIP signaling (port 5060) and RTP media (port range 10000-20000) traffic originates from the Verasist server
  • Most providers reject traffic from unknown IPs for security reasons
  • If your Verasist instance IP changes, you must update the whitelist with your provider
Steps:
  1. Find your Verasist server's public IP address
  2. Log in to your SIP trunk provider's dashboard (e.g. NetGSM's management panel)
  3. Navigate to security / IP whitelist / allowed IPs settings
  4. Add your Verasist server's public IP
  5. Wait for the change to propagate (usually instant, but can take a few minutes)

Inbound Calling Setup

Inbound calls use the same org-wide webhook URL as other telephony providers:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run

DID Routing

Your SIP trunk provider must route incoming calls to the Verasist server. The setup varies by provider:

  1. DID Routing: In your provider's dashboard, configure each DID/phone number to forward incoming calls to the Verasist server's IP address. Some providers call this "DID forwarding", "call routing", or "destination configuration".
  2. SIP Registration: If your trunk uses registration (register: true), incoming calls are automatically routed to the registered endpoint. No additional DID routing is needed.
  3. IP Authentication: If your trunk uses IP-based auth (register: false), make sure the provider knows to send calls to your Verasist server IP.

Assign an Inbound Workflow

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI voice agent answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in the Verasist dashboard

Provider-Specific Notes

NetGSM

NetGSM is a Turkish SIP trunk provider. Key setup details:

  • IP Whitelisting: After obtaining your trunk credentials, log in to the NetGSM customer panel and add the Verasist server IP to the allowed IP list (usually found under "Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama" or similar)
  • DID Routing: Configure each DID to forward to the Verasist server IP under "Santral" → "Yönlendirme"
  • Registration: NetGSM requires SIP registration (register: true)
  • Gateway: The gateway address (e.g. sip.netgsm.com.tr) is provided in your NetGSM welcome email
  • Codec: NetGSM supports G.711 (alaw/ulaw)

Verimor

Verimor is a Turkish SIP trunk and call management provider. Key setup details:

  • IP Whitelisting: Add the Verasist server IP to Verimor's allowed IP list through the customer panel
  • Registration: Verimor requires SIP registration (register: true)
  • Gateway: The gateway address is provided in your Verimor account details
  • DID Routing: Configure DID forwarding to the Verasist server IP in the Verimor panel

Twilio Elastic SIP Trunking

  • Create an Elastic SIP Trunk in the Twilio console
  • Configure the trunk's termination URI to point to the Verasist server IP
  • Twilio uses IP-based authentication by default — make sure your trunk's "Authentication" is configured correctly
  • Set register: false in Verasist for IP-based auth

Other Providers

For Flowroute, Vobiz, or any other SIP trunk provider, the process is similar:

  1. Obtain SIP credentials from the provider
  2. Whitelist the Verasist server IP on the provider's side
  3. Configure DID routing for inbound calls
  4. Enter the gateway IP/username/password in Verasist's SIP configuration

Troubleshooting

Overview

Agent Stream is a WebSocket endpoint that lets a telephony provider point its media stream at a single URL and drive a Verasist agent run. The agent UUID in the URL selects the agent; provider-specific identifiers in the query string (for Cloudonix: Domain) tell Verasist which stored telephony configuration to use for that call. The bearer token and other credentials are never passed in the URL — they live in the stored configuration and are used by Verasist to validate the session and to issue provider API calls (hangup, transfer) during the call.

This is useful when:

  • You're integrating Verasist into a SIP gateway or in-house dialer that already speaks a supported provider's streaming protocol
  • You want one stable endpoint per agent rather than wiring up an inbound webhook per phone number
Agent Stream currently supports the Cloudonix provider only. Other providers return NotImplementedError until a per-provider implementation lands. If you need Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Vonage, ARI, or another provider, please open a request on GitHub Discussions with your use case.

Endpoint

wss://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/agent-stream/{agent_uuid}
{agent_uuid} is the agent's stable UUID (see Get the Agent UUID below).

Prerequisites

  • A Verasist agent (workflow) — published or in draft is fine
  • A Cloudonix telephony configuration in your Verasist organization whose domain_id matches the Domain you pass on the URL. Verasist uses the bearer token from this configuration to validate the call session and to issue provider API calls (hangup, transfer).

Get the Agent UUID

The Agent UUID is the workflow's stable identifier — it doesn't change when versions are published.

To find and copy it in the UI, see Agent UUID.

Connect to the WebSocket

URL parameters

Param Required Description
provider Yes Provider name. Currently only cloudonix is supported.
Domain Yes (cloudonix) Cloudonix domain ID. Verasist uses this to look up the matching stored telephony configuration and retrieve the bearer token used for provider API calls.
callId / CallSid No Call identifier from your side; persisted on the workflow run's gathered_context as call_id. The Cloudonix call SID used for streaming is taken from the start event payload, not this param.
from No Caller phone number, persisted on the workflow run as caller_number.
to No Called phone number, persisted on the workflow run as called_number.

Cloudonix example

wss://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/agent-stream/{agent_uuid}
  ?provider=cloudonix
  &Domain={CLOUDONIX_DOMAIN_ID}
  &callId={CALL_ID}
  &from=+15555550100
  &to=+15555550199

Use this URL inside the CXML your Cloudonix Voice Application returns when the call needs to be bridged to the Verasist agent:

The first two messages on the socket should be Cloudonix's standard connected and start events (Twilio-compatible framing). Verasist extracts streamSid and callSid from the start event payload, validates the session against Cloudonix using the bearer token from the stored telephony configuration matched by Domain, and then begins streaming audio.

Workflow run lifecycle

When the WebSocket is accepted, Verasist:

  1. Looks up the workflow by agent_uuid
  2. Runs a quota check against the workflow's owning user
  3. Creates a new WorkflowRun (call_type=inbound, mode=cloudonix, name WR-AGS-XXXXXXXX) with the from/to numbers stamped on initial_context, the callId/CallSid stored as call_id on gathered_context, and Domain recorded under the run's inbound_webhook log
  4. Transitions the run to running and starts the agent pipeline
The run is visible under the agent's Runs tab as soon as it's minted, just like an inbound or outbound call.

Close codes

Code Reason
1008 Routing failure — unknown provider, workflow not found, or quota exceeded
1011 Server-side failure or unsupported provider for Agent Stream
4400 Provider-level handshake error — for cloudonix, missing Domain, no matching telephony configuration, missing bearer token on the configuration, malformed connected/start events, or session validation failed against Cloudonix

Security notes

  • Treat the URL as a secret — the agent UUID itself authorizes the connection. Store and transmit it only over TLS, and avoid logging the raw URL in places where access is broader than your operations team.
  • No bearer tokens or provider secrets are passed in the URL. Provider credentials live in the stored telephony configuration (matched by Domain for Cloudonix) and are used server-side by Verasist to validate the session and issue provider API calls.

Overview

Verasist AI supports multiple messaging channels through a unified channel configuration system. Each channel uses the same infrastructure — configure once, and your AI agents can handle both chat and voice interactions across all connected platforms.

Supported Channels

Messaging Channels

Channels that support two-way conversations (inbound messages and replies):

WhatsApp Cloud API for chat messaging and voice calling via Business Calling API Telegram Bot API for chat messaging Instagram Messaging API for direct messages

Content-Publishing Channels

Channels that let your agents publish content (no inbound messaging). Each has a matching built-in tool:

Publish posts and manage comments on a Facebook Page Publish text, image, and video posts to a LinkedIn profile Publish videos to a TikTok creator account Publish posts and read replies on a Threads profile Publish posts, reply, and read replies on an X account Publish and manage blog posts on a WordPress site
Content-publishing channels are content-only — they have no webhook and don't receive inbound messages. They are used exclusively through their built-in post tools. See the tools reference for details.

How Channels Work

All messaging channels follow the same pattern:

  1. Configure: Enter your channel credentials (API tokens, keys) in the Verasist UI under /channels
  2. Webhook Registration: Verasist provides a webhook URL that you register with the channel platform
  3. Inbound Messages: When a user sends a message, the platform sends a webhook to Verasist
  4. Agent Processing: Verasist routes the message to your AI agent's workflow
  5. Reply: The agent's response is sent back through the same channel

Shared Webhook Endpoint

Each channel type has its own webhook endpoint:

Channel Webhook URL
WhatsApp https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/whatsapp/webhook
Telegram https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/telegram/webhook
Instagram https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/instagram/webhook

Configuration

All channel configurations are managed from a single page:

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration (or use the Quick Connect cards)
  2. Select the channel type — messaging (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram) or content (Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, Threads, X, WordPress)
  3. Enter the required credentials — OAuth for most social channels, an Application Password for WordPress
  4. Save and register the webhook URL with the platform (messaging channels only)

Capabilities

Channel Chat Voice Webhook Auth
WhatsApp ✅ ✅ X-Hub-Signature-256 (SHA-256 HMAC)
Telegram ✅ ❌ X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header
Instagram ✅ ❌ X-Hub-Signature-256 (SHA-256 HMAC)

Troubleshooting

Webhook not receiving events- Verify the webhook URL is publicly accessible from the internet - Check that the webhook is registered correctly in the platform's developer dashboard - Ensure the channel configuration is saved in Verasist
Webhook verification failing- Confirm the verify token / webhook secret matches between Verasist and the platform - For Meta platforms (WhatsApp, Instagram), ensure the app secret is configured for signature validation - Check for proxy or load balancer modifications to the request
Messages not sending- Verify the access token / bot token is valid and not expired - Check that the target user ID is correct - Ensure the account has the necessary permissions (e.g., WhatsApp Business account verified)

Overview

Verasist AI integrates with WhatsApp through Meta's Cloud API and Business Calling API. Once configured, your AI agents can:

  • Chat: Send and receive WhatsApp messages automatically
  • Voice: Make and receive WhatsApp voice calls via WebRTC
The WhatsApp integration uses Meta's Graph API infrastructure. All communication flows through Meta's servers — Verasist acts as the AI brain that processes messages and calls.

Prerequisites

  • A Meta Business App created in the Meta Developer Dashboard
  • A WhatsApp Business Account linked to your Meta app
  • A verified phone number for WhatsApp Business
  • The following credentials from Meta:
- Permanent Access Token — Generated from your Meta app's WhatsApp settings - Phone Number ID — The ID of your WhatsApp Business phone number - Verify Token — A custom token you create for webhook verification - App Secret (optional but recommended) — For webhook signature validation

Configuration

Step 1: Set Up Meta App

  1. Go to developers.facebook.com and create a new app (or use an existing one)
  2. Add the WhatsApp product to your app
  3. Under WhatsApp → API Setup, note your:
- Phone Number ID - WhatsApp Business Account ID
  1. Generate a Permanent Access Token from System Users or via the WhatsApp settings

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select WhatsApp as the channel type
  3. Fill in the credentials:
Field Description
Name A display name for this configuration (e.g. "WhatsApp Prod")
Access Token WhatsApp Cloud API permanent access token
Phone Number ID Your WhatsApp Business phone number ID from Meta
Verify Token A custom token for webhook verification — create any string and use the same value in Meta's webhook config
App Secret Meta App Secret from App Settings → Basic. Used for X-Hub-Signature-256 validation (recommended)
Graph API Version Meta Graph API version (default: v21.0)
Enabled Capabilities Select "Chat" and/or "Voice"
  1. Click Save Configuration

Step 3: Register Webhook with Meta

  1. In your Meta app dashboard, go to WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhook
  2. Set the Callback URL to:
   https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/whatsapp/webhook
  1. Set the Verify Token to the same value you entered in Verasist
  2. Click Verify and Save
  3. Under Webhook Fields, subscribe to at least:
- messages — for incoming chat messages - message_template_status — if using templates
The webhook URL must be publicly accessible for Meta to send events.

Chat Messaging

Once configured, incoming WhatsApp messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a WhatsApp message to your business number
  2. Meta sends a webhook to Verasist with the message content
  3. Verasist matches the webhook to your organization and channel config
  4. Your AI agent's workflow processes the message and generates a reply
  5. The reply is sent back through the WhatsApp Cloud API

Voice Calling

WhatsApp voice calling uses Meta's Business Calling API (WebRTC-based):

  1. An outbound call is initiated from the Verasist UI or via API
  2. Verasist creates a WebRTC session through Meta's calling infrastructure
  3. Audio streams between the caller and your AI agent in real time
  4. The voice pipeline handles speech-to-text, LLM reasoning, and text-to-speech
To enable voice calling, select both Chat and Voice in the Enabled Capabilities field.
WhatsApp voice calling requires additional Meta business verification and approval. Refer to Meta's Business Calling API documentation for prerequisites and limitations.

Webhook Security

Verasist validates incoming WhatsApp webhooks using:

  1. Verify Token (hub.verify_token): Used during initial webhook registration (GET challenge)
  2. App Secret (X-Hub-Signature-256): SHA-256 HMAC signature of the request body. If configured, Verasist validates every POST webhook against this signature
It's strongly recommended to configure the App Secret for production use.

Inbound Message Flow

WhatsApp User → Meta Server → Webhook → Verasist → Agent Workflow → Reply → Meta API → WhatsApp User

The from_identity in the webhook payload is the user's WhatsApp phone number (e.g. +905321234567), which is used to track conversations and maintain context.

Test Your Integration

  1. Save your WhatsApp configuration in Verasist
  2. Register the webhook URL in Meta's dashboard and verify it succeeds
  3. Send a test WhatsApp message to your business number
  4. Check that your AI agent responds
  5. Check call logs in the Verasist dashboard for any errors

Troubleshooting

Webhook verification fails- Ensure the Verify Token in Verasist exactly matches the token set in Meta's webhook config - Confirm the callback URL is publicly accessible (Meta performs a GET request to it) - Check that your server's firewall allows inbound HTTPS traffic
Messages not being received- Verify you subscribed to the messages webhook field in Meta's dashboard - Check that the phone number is connected to your WhatsApp Business Account - Ensure the access token has whatsapp_business_messaging permission
Messages not sending- Verify the access token is still valid (not expired) - Check that the recipient's phone number is in the correct format - Ensure the WhatsApp Business account has not hit rate limits
Voice calls not connecting- Confirm "Voice" is enabled in the configuration's capabilities - Ensure the access token has whatsapp_business_voice permission - Verify the phone number supports voice calling (requires business verification)

Overview

Verasist AI integrates with Telegram through the Telegram Bot API. Once configured, your AI agents can automatically handle Telegram conversations — answering questions, processing requests, and engaging users directly in Telegram chats.

The Telegram integration is chat-only (Telegram Bot API does not support public voice calling for bots).

Prerequisites

  • A Telegram bot created via @BotFather
  • Your bot's Bot Token (obtained from BotFather)

Configuration

Step 1: Create a Telegram Bot

  1. Open Telegram and message @BotFather
  2. Send /newbot and follow the prompts to create your bot
  3. Save the Bot Token provided by BotFather (format: 123456789:ABCdefGHIjklMNOpqrsTUVwxyz)
  4. Optionally, set a profile picture and description with /setuserpic and /setdescription

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select Telegram as the channel type
  3. Fill in the credentials:
Field Description
Name A display name for this configuration (e.g. "Telegram Bot")
Bot Token Your Telegram bot token from @BotFather
Webhook Secret Token A custom secret for X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token validation (recommended)
  1. Click Save Configuration

Step 3: Set the Webhook

Unlike Meta platforms, Telegram does not use a GET challenge for webhook verification. Instead, you register the webhook URL via the Bot API setWebhook method:

curl -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot/setWebhook" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/telegram/webhook",
    "secret_token": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET"
  }'

Replace:

  • with your bot token
  • YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET with the webhook secret you configured in Verasist
Verify the webhook was set:

curl "https://api.telegram.org/bot/getWebhookInfo"
The webhook URL must be publicly accessible (HTTPS required by Telegram).

How It Works

Once configured, incoming Telegram messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a message to your Telegram bot
  2. Telegram sends a webhook to Verasist with the message update
  3. Verasist validates the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header (if configured)
  4. The webhook is matched to your organization and channel config
  5. Your AI agent's workflow processes the message and generates a reply
  6. The reply is sent back through the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage)

Message Flow

Telegram User → Telegram Server → Webhook → Verasist → Agent Workflow → Reply → Bot API → Telegram User

The from_identity used for conversation tracking is the user's Telegram chat_id.

Webhook Security

Verasist validates incoming Telegram webhooks using:

  • X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header: If you set a webhook_secret in the Verasist configuration, every incoming webhook is validated against this header. Telegram includes this header in every webhook request if set during setWebhook.
It's strongly recommended to configure the webhook secret for production use.

Supported Update Types

The Telegram integration handles:

  • Text messages (message with text field)
  • Direct messages and group mentions (when the bot is mentioned with @botname)
Unsupported update types (ignored silently):
  • edited_message
  • callback_query
  • inline_query
  • Photos, videos, documents, and other non-text media
  • Channel posts

Test Your Integration

  1. Save your Telegram configuration in Verasist
  2. Run the setWebhook command to register your webhook URL
  3. Verify with getWebhookInfo — you should see "ok": true and "url" pointing to Verasist
  4. Send a message to your bot on Telegram
  5. Check that your AI agent responds
  6. Check the Verasist dashboard for any errors

Troubleshooting

Webhook not receiving events- Run getWebhookInfo to check if the webhook URL is set correctly - Verify the webhook URL uses HTTPS (Telegram requires HTTPS) - Ensure there are no pending updates: getWebhookInfo shows pending_update_count - Check that your server's firewall allows inbound HTTPS from Telegram's IPs
Secret token validation fails- Ensure the webhook_secret in Verasist matches the secret_token sent in setWebhook - Re-run setWebhook if you changed the secret
Bot not responding- Verify the bot token is valid and the bot is not blocked by the user - Check that there's at least one workflow in your organization - Ensure the workflow has an agent node configured - Check the Verasist logs for pipeline errors
Messages sending slowly- Telegram Bot API has rate limits (~30 messages/second per chat) - Check network latency between Verasist and api.telegram.org - The LLM inference time is the dominant factor in response latency

How It Works

Once configured, incoming Instagram Direct Messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a Direct Message to your Instagram Business account

Feature Instagram WhatsApp

Overview

Verasist exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI assistants like Codex, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and Cursor access your workspace and documentation. Once connected, an assistant can list your agents, fetch agent definitions, and search Verasist docs on your behalf.

Prerequisites

  • A Verasist API key. Generate one at /api-keys. See API Keys.
  • Your Verasist MCP endpoint:
- Hosted: https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/

The endpoint is also shown in Platform Settings → MCP Server inside the Verasist UI.

Claude Code

Register Verasist as an MCP server with the Claude Code CLI:

claude mcp add --transport http verasist https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/ \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

Replace YOUR_API_KEY with the key you generated.

Verify the server is connected:

claude mcp list

Codex

Open Codex's config file (~/.codex/config.toml) and add a verasist MCP server:

[mcp_servers.verasist]
url = "https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/"
http_headers = { "X-API-Key" = "YOUR_API_KEY" }

Replace YOUR_API_KEY with the key you generated.

If you prefer to keep the API key out of config.toml, store it in an environment variable instead:

[mcp_servers.verasist]
url = "https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/"
env_http_headers = { "X-API-Key" = "VERASIST_API_KEY" }

Then set the API key before starting Codex:

export VERASIST_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
codex

Verify the server is registered:

codex mcp list
codex mcp get verasist

Claude Desktop

Open Claude Desktop's config file (claude_desktop_config.json) and add the verasist entry under mcpServers:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "verasist": {
      "url": "https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-Key": "YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop after saving. The Verasist tools should appear in the tool picker.

Cursor and other MCP clients

Any MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP transport can connect with the same URL and header. Paste the configuration above into your client's MCP settings file and replace YOUR_API_KEY.

Example prompts

Once the MCP server is connected, you can drive Verasist from your coding agent in plain English. A few prompts to try:

Explore your workspace
  • "List my agents in Verasist."
  • "Show me the definition of the agent called Lead Qualifier."
  • "Which credentials and tools are configured in my Verasist workspace?"
  • "List the recordings from my most recent agent."
Edit an agent
  • "In my Lead Qualifier agent, add a new agent node after the greeting that asks the caller for their budget, then routes to the existing qualification node."
  • "Add an end-call node to Support Bot that triggers when the user says they are done, with a polite goodbye prompt."
  • "Rename the intro node in Lead Qualifier to greeting and update any edges that reference it."
  • "Change the LLM model on all agent nodes in Support Bot to gpt-4o-mini."
Learn the platform
  • "Search the Verasist docs for how to connect SDK tools to a workflow node."
  • "What node types does Verasist support, and what fields does a knowledge_base node take?"
  • "How do I deploy Verasist on a custom domain with HTTPS?"
Agent edits are saved as a new draft version — your published agent keeps serving calls until you explicitly publish the draft from the Verasist UI.
The API key controls which workspace the assistant sees. Treat it like any other credential — do not commit it to source control or paste it into shared chats.

How Model Configuration Works

Verasist bundles the AI services an agent needs — LLM, voice (TTS), transcriber (STT), and optionally a single speech-to-speech Realtime model — into a single reusable preset called an Assistant (also called a model package). Assistants are curated by your platform administrator; as an organization user, you don't pick an LLM, a voice, and a transcriber one by one — you pick an Assistant, and it brings all of those services with it.

Each Assistant card in the catalog shows the properties that matter for choosing one: cost tier, speed tier, voice gender, accent, speaking style, and language.

Verasist uses a two-level assignment system for Assistants:

  1. Organization default — the Assistant every workflow uses unless it has its own assignment.
  2. Per-workflow assignment — an optional override that points a specific workflow at a different Assistant.
If a workflow has no assignment of its own, it falls back to the organization default.
Credentials (API keys, service-account JSON, and other account-level fields) for each inference provider are managed centrally by your platform administrator, not by individual organizations — they're wired up once behind the scenes when an Assistant is created. Admins manage these credentials under Admin > Provider Credentials (/provider-credentials) and manage the Assistant catalog under Admin > Model Packages.

Choosing Your Organization's Default Assistant

Overview

Tracing gives you full visibility into what happened during a test call or live call. It's one of the most powerful features for making your voice agents production-ready.

With traces, you can see:

  • The exact conversation that occurred
  • What prompts were sent to the LLM
  • Which tools the LLM had access to (and which it called)
  • Speech-to-text transcriptions of user input and Transcription errors
  • Tool call requests and responses

Accessing Traces

After a call ends, you'll see a call summary screen. Click the Traces tab to view the detailed trace log for that call.

Understanding Trace Sections

Traces are organized by event type. The two most important sections to focus on are:

STT (Speech-to-Text)

These entries capture the transcription of what the user said during the call. Each STT entry shows the text conversion of the user's speech at that point in the conversation.

Example:

STT: "Yeah, I would want to check what your operating hours are."

LLM (Language Model Calls)

These entries show every call made to the LLM. Each LLM trace includes:

  • Prompt - The full prompt sent to the LLM (combination of global prompt + node-specific prompt)
  • Conversation history - The entire conversation up to that point
  • Available tools - All tools the LLM can access for that node
  • Response - What the LLM generated

Tools in Traces

Each LLM call shows the tools available to the agent at that moment. These fall into three categories:

System Tools (Default)

Every node includes these by default:

  • Safe Calculator — Helps LLMs perform math accurately
  • Get Current Time — Retrieves current time
  • Convert Time — Converts time to a specific timezone

Pathway Tools

These correspond to the pathways (node transitions) you've configured. For example, if your node has pathways to "End Call" and "Move to Summary," you'll see those as available tools.

The tool descriptions shown in traces match the descriptions you set in your pathway configuration.

Custom Tools

Any external tools you've attached to the node (e.g. any custom tools you created for API endpoints for booking, order submission, etc.) will appear here. See the custom tools documentation.

Tool Calls in Traces

When the LLM decides to call a tool, you'll see:

  1. Tool call request — The tool name and parameters sent
  2. Tool response — The result returned (e.g., {"status": "ok"})
The tool call and response also appear in subsequent conversation history, so the LLM knows the outcome. Example flow: User: "Can you book me a table for tomorrow at 7pm?" LLM calls: book_table(date: "tomorrow", time: "7pm", party_size: 2) Tool response: ``{"status": "done", "confirmation": "Table booked"}` Agent: "I've booked your table for tomorrow at 7pm."

How Prompts Are Combined

The prompt sent to the LLM is a combination of:

  1. Global Prompt — Defined in your Global Node settings
  2. Node Prompt — Defined in the specific node being executed
If you disable the Global Node for a particular node, only the node-specific prompt will be used.

Key Concept: Conversation History

Every time an LLM call is made, the entire conversation history up to that point is passed to the LLM. This means:

  • The LLM always has full context
  • You can see exactly what context the LLM had when it made a decision
  • Useful for debugging unexpected responses

Setting Up Langfuse Tracing

We provide seamless integration with Langfuse for tracing if you want to use your own account. This enables you to use the playground feature of Langfuse.

Setup steps:
  1. Sign up at Langfuse and create API credentials
  2. In the Verasist UI, go to Platform Settings (/settings) and enter your Langfuse host, public key, and secret key
  3. Click Save
Once enabled, traces will be available for every completed call in Verasist.

Quick Reference

Trace Type What It Shows
STT User speech transcribed to text
LLM Prompt + conversation + tools + response
Tool Call Tool invocation and response

Tips for Using Traces

  • Debug unexpected responses — Check the LLM trace to see what prompt and context the model received
  • Verify tool calls — Confirm tools are being triggered with correct parameters
  • Refine prompts — Use traces to see how your prompt instructions affect LLM behavior
  • Check transcription accuracy — Review STT entries if the agent misunderstands users

The current API version is v1. The version is included in the URL path.

Request format

All request bodies must be sent as JSON with the Content-Type: application/json header.

curl -X POST https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/workflow/create/definition \

All responses are JSON. Successful responses return the relevant resource object. Error responses follow a consistent shape:

{

{
  "detail": [

    }
  ]
}

The API Tetikleyici düğüm lets you initiate outbound calls to your sesli asistan programmatically. When you add an API Tetikleyici düğüm to your iş akışı, Verasist generates a unique endpoint URL that external systems can call to start a conversation.

This is useful when you want to tetikleyici calls from your own backend, a CRM, or iş akışı araçlar like n8n and Zapier.

Prerequisites

  • A configured telephony provider — outbound calls will fail without one
  • An API key for authentication

Finding your tetikleyici URL

When you add an API Tetikleyici düğüm to your iş akışı, Verasist assigns it a unique UUID. The tetikleyici düğüm exposes two URLs that share this UUID:

  • A production URL for the published iş akışı
  • A test URL for the latest draft
You can copy either URL from the tetikleyici düğüm's settings dialog. 
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid}        # Production
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid}   # Test

If you are using the hosted version, replace verasist.ai with api.verasist.ai.

Test vs production

Mode URL Runs
Production /api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} The published version of the agent.
Test /api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} The latest draft. Falls back to the published version if no draft exists.

Use the test URL while iterating on changes so production traffic continues to hit the published version.

The production URL only executes a published iş akışı. If you update the iş akışı but do not publish it, the production tetikleyici will continue to run the older published version.

Once you publish your draft, both URLs run the same definition.

A common pitfall is editing the iş akışı, saving the draft, and then calling the production tetikleyici URL expecting the new behavior. That will not work until you publish the iş akışı. Use the test URL to verify draft changes before publishing.

The request body, headers, and response shape are identical for both URLs.

Channels

By default, an API Tetikleyici düğüm launches a phone call, but the düğüm can be configured for a different channel — whatsapp, telegram, instagram, or text — and a request can override that channel per call by passing channel in the request body.

channel Required request fields Response message
phone (default) phone_number null
whatsapp / telegram / instagram target (destination identity for that channel), channel_configuration_id (unless the düğüm has one configured) The iş akışı's first generated reply
text — The iş akışı's first generated reply
text starts the iş akışı without any external channel — the response body itself contains the agent's first message, useful for embedding the agent in your own UI without setting up a channel integration.

``bash WhatsApp channel curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "channel": "whatsapp", "target": "+14155550100", "channel_configuration_id": 12, "initial_context": {"customer_name": "Jane"} }' 


channel is required in the request body when neither the düğüm nor the request otherwise specify one — for example when tetikleyiciing by iş akışı UUID directly, which has no düğüm to fall back to.


Making a request


Authenticate by passing your API key in the X-API-Key header. For the default phone channel, the request body requires a phone_number and accepts optional initial_context and telephony_configuration_id fields (see Channels above for the fields required by other channels).
bash Production URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }'
bash Test URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }'

Overview

Vonage (formerly Nexmo) is a cloud communications platform that provides global voice, messaging, and video capabilities. Verasist AI's Vonage integration enables high-quality voice interactions with your asistanlar using Vonage's robust infrastructure.

Prerequisites

Before setting up Vonage integration, you'll need:

  • A Vonage account
  • Vonage Application with Voice capability enabled
  • Application ID and Private Key from your Vonage Dashboard
  • API Key and API Secret from your Vonage Dashboard
  • At least one Vonage phone number linked to the application
  • Verasist AI instance running and accessible

Configuration

Step 1: Create Vonage Application

  1. Log in to your Vonage Dashboard
  2. Navigate to Applications → Create a new application
  3. Enable Voice capability
  4. Generate a private key (save this securely - you'll need it)
  5. Note your Application ID

Step 2: Get API Credentials

  1. Find your API Key and API Secret in the dashboard under API Settings
  2. Navigate to Numbers → Your Numbers
  3. Copy your phone number(s)
  4. Link your numbers to your application

Step 3: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select Vonage as your provider
  3. Enter your credentials:
- Application ID - Private Key (entire key including BEGIN/END lines) - API Key - API Secret
  1. Click Save Configuration
  2. Open the configuration you just created and add at least one phone number (without + prefix, e.g. 14155551234). The default caller ID is used for outbound calls.

Step 4: Test Your Configuration

  1. Create a test iş akışı
  2. Click "Call" to verify connection
  3. Check call logs for successful connection

Inbound Calling Setup

Vonage configures inbound web kancaları at the application level, not per phone number. A single Answer URL on the Vonage application applies to every number linked to it. Verasist routes the call to the right agent based on the called number's inbound iş akışı assignment inside Verasist. When you save an inbound iş akışı on a phone number, Verasist automatically pushes the web kancası URL to your Vonage Application's Answer URL (provided the credentials are correct).

Step 1: Link Phone Numbers to Your Vonage Application

  1. Open the Vonage Dashboard
  2. Under Numbers → Your Numbers, link each number you want to use for inbound to the same Vonage Application whose ID you configured in Verasist

Step 2: Assign an Inbound İş Akışı to the Phone Number in Verasist

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your Vonage configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound iş akışı to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Step 3: Verify the Answer URL on the Vonage Application

  1. Open your Vonage Application in the Vonage Dashboard
  2. Under Capabilities → Voice, confirm:
- Answer URL is set to: https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - HTTP Method is POST
Verasist pushed this URL automatically when you saved the inbound iş akışı in Step 2. If the field is empty, shows a different URL, or Verasist surfaced a sync warning on save, the auto-push failed — most often because the API Key/Secret or Application ID in Verasist is incorrect. Paste the URL into the field yourself, set the method to POST, and save the application.

Overview

Telnyx is a cloud communications platform that provides programmable voice via its Call Control API. Verasist AI's Telnyx integration uses Call Control plus WebSocket media streaming to power your sesli asistans.

Prerequisites

Before setting up Telnyx integration, you'll need:

  • A Telnyx account
  • An API Key from the Telnyx Mission Control Portal
  • A Call Control Application (optional — leave the field blank in Verasist and we'll auto-create one for you on save, with the inbound web kancası URL pre-set)
  • At least one Telnyx phone number assigned to that Call Control Application
  • Verasist AI instance running and accessible

Configuration

Step 1: Get Telnyx Credentials

  1. Log in to the Telnyx Mission Control Portal
  2. Navigate to API Keys and create (or copy) an API Key
  3. (Optional) Navigate to Call Control → Applications and create (or open) the application you'll use with Verasist, then copy its Connection ID (Call Control App ID). Skip this if you want Verasist to auto-create the Call Control Application for you on save.
  4. Navigate to Numbers → My Numbers and assign your phone numbers to the Call Control Application you'll use with Verasist (if you're letting Verasist auto-create the application, do this after saving the configuration in Step 2)

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select Telnyx as your provider
  3. Enter your credentials:
- API Key - Call Control App ID (Connection ID) — optional. Leave blank and Verasist will auto-create a Call Control Application on save (with the inbound web kancası URL already configured) and store its Connection ID on this configuration.
  1. Click Save Configuration
  2. Open the configuration you just created and add at least one phone number (with country code in E.164 format, e.g. +1234567890). The default caller ID is used for outbound calls.
If Verasist auto-created the Call Control Application for you, you still need to assign your Telnyx numbers to that application in the Telnyx Portal under Numbers → My Numbers. The auto-created application is named verasist- — its Connection ID is shown on the saved configuration.

Step 3: Test Your Configuration

  1. Create a test iş akışı
  2. Click "Call" to verify connection
  3. Check call logs for successful connection

Inbound Calling Setup

Telnyx delivers inbound web kancaları at the Call Control Application level — the web kancası URL is configured once on the application, and applies to every number assigned to it. When you save an inbound iş akışı on a phone number, Verasist automatically pushes the web kancası URL to your Call Control Application's web kancası_event_url (provided the credentials are correct). If Verasist auto-created the application during configuration save, the web kancası URL is already set and this step is a no-op.

Step 1: Assign an Inbound İş Akışı to the Phone Number

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your Telnyx configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound iş akışı to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Step 2: Verify the Web Kancası URL on the Call Control Application

  1. Go to Call Control → Applications in the Telnyx Portal
  2. Open the application whose Connection ID you configured in Verasist
  3. In Web Kancası Settings, confirm:
- Web Kancası URL is set to: https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run - HTTP Method is POST
  1. Make sure the phone numbers you want to use for inbound are assigned to this application
Verasist pushed this URL automatically when you saved the inbound iş akışı in Step 1. The same URL is shared across every number on the Call Control Application — Verasist matches the inbound call to the right agent using the called number's inbound iş akışı assignment. If the field is empty, shows a different URL, or Verasist surfaced a sync warning on save, the auto-push failed — most often because the API Key or Connection ID in Verasist is incorrect. Paste the URL into the field yourself, set the method to POST, and save.

Step 3: Verify Setup

  • Ensure your Verasist AI instance is publicly accessible
  • Verify any firewalls allow Telnyx's IP ranges

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured Telnyx phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI sesli asistan answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in both Verasist AI dashboard and Telnyx Portal

NetGSM

NetGSM, Türk SIP trunk sağlayıcısıdır. Temel kurulum ayrıntıları:

  • IP Whitelisting: Trunk kimlik bilgilerinizi aldıktan sonra NetGSM müşteri paneline giriş yapın ve Verasist sunucu IP'sini izin verilen IP listesine ekleyin (genellikle "Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama" veya benzeri altında bulunur)
